strings.name: Wes McKinney
strings.summary: Wes McKinney created pandas, co-created Apache Arrow and taught data-analysis practices through Python for Data Analysis. His work addresses cross-language data exchange and sustainable open-source maintenance. He is the founder of Kenn Software and a Principal Architect at Posit. Subsequent pandas development depends on maintainers and the community, not solely its creator.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Development began in 2008; open sourcing followed in 2009. Doctoral study is not a completed doctorate. Sources differ on his MIT graduation year, so no precise year is asserted.
strings.influence.rationale: Created pandas and contributed to Apache Arrow, advancing Python data analysis and cross-system data exchange.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied mathematics at MIT, then entered Duke’s statistical-science PhD program, leaving in 2011 to focus on open source.
strings.facts.f2.label: Key projects
strings.facts.f2.value: Created pandas and Ibis and co-created Apache Arrow, with teams and communities contributing to their development.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Python data-analysis tools
strings.highlights.h1.text: Created pandas for working with tabular data; a community continues its development.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Cross-system data exchange
strings.highlights.h2.text: Helped create Apache Arrow to share columnar in-memory data across languages and systems.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Founds Kenn Software
strings.timeline.t1.text: His website dates its founding to this year; the company identifies him as team leader. He continues his Posit role.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Posit announces his arrival
strings.timeline.t2.text: The welcome announcement confirms he has joined. His website lists his current Principal Architect role and Python/AI strategy work.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Third edition of his textbook published
strings.timeline.t3.text: Python for Data Analysis’s third edition first appears. Its online reading edition does not give the prose a freely reusable open license.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Announces Ursa Labs
strings.timeline.t4.text: Announces collaboration with RStudio and Two Sigma to support cross-language open-source data-science infrastructure.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Apache Arrow publicly announced
strings.timeline.t5.text: ASF announces Arrow as a top-level project and quotes him; it is a collaboration among developers from many projects.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First data-analysis textbook published
strings.timeline.t6.text: His GitHub interview dates the first edition of Python for Data Analysis to this month.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leaves doctoral study for open source
strings.timeline.t7.text: Takes leave and ultimately drops out of Duke’s PhD program to concentrate on pandas.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Starts developing pandas
strings.timeline.t8.text: Begins the project while working at AQR; it becomes open source by the end of 2009.
